metadata.title: Populating Next Right Pointers in Each Node II

problem_summary.summary: Set each node's next reference to the next node on its level, or null at the level's end, for an arbitrary binary tree.
problem_summary.input_output: Input: root of a binary tree using Node with left, right, and next links. Return root after setting next links.
constraints: Initially every next link is null

brute_force.explanation: Perform breadth-first traversal and connect consecutive nodes within each queue level.
brute_force.correctness_idea: The queue contains exactly one tree level at the start of each iteration, so linking its nodes in removal order assigns every next pointer to the correct same-level neighbor.
brute_force.time_complexity: O(n) — each node is visited once.
brute_force.space_complexity: O(w) auxiliary queue space, where w is maximum level width.

optimized.explanation: Use already-built next links to scan a level, while a dummy head and tail collect the next level's existing children from left to right.
optimized.correctness_idea: Scanning the current level by next visits nodes in left-to-right order. Appending each present child in that order builds precisely the next level's chain; resetting the dummy for each level prevents stale links.
optimized.time_complexity: O(n) — each node is scanned once while its level is processed.
optimized.space_complexity: O(1) auxiliary, excluding the returned tree; only a dummy node and pointers are used.

steps.action: Append both children to the dummy-headed next-level chain.

steps.event: Scan level 2 through existing next links.
steps.action: Append each child; 4.next=5, 5.next=7, and tail 7.next remains null.
No next-level child is collected; traversal ends.

edge_cases.handling: The loop does not start and null is returned.
Only existing children are appended, preserving their left-to-right order.
Its next pointer remains null and there is no next level.
